ACCEPTThe theorem is correct under the explicitly stated full- $U$ /standard-rotor square-lattice model and conditional on the existence of a complete extension containing  $H$ .The complete-extension qualifier is essential. Endpoint-disjoint partial owners with a leg tip above row  $30$  do exist, but none can survive the recursively forced owner at the next support. The theorem does not establish existence of a complete extension, catalogue exhaustion for arbitrary grids, global monotonicity, or the global  $5/6$  improvement.1. Recursive source geometryExpanding the supplied independent_source, chain, old_chain, receiver, consumer, rotor, and south- $U$  constructors gives the following all-parameter facts for even  $h\ge 12$ ,  $g\ge4$ :The old recursive inventory has no endpoint in column  $C=h+13$  at rows  $23,\ldots,30$ .Its maximum endpoint column is  $C+6$ .The row- $22$  old union is exactly the contiguous  $W$ -segment from  $-34$  through  $6$ .After adding  $A$ , the row- $22$  union is exactly
$$[-34,6]\cup[7,b]=[-34,b].$$
The lower recursive blocks do not introduce endpoints in the far columns  $J\le -36$ , regardless of their unbounded depths.The row-local consequence needed for the east case is also true: endpoints of  $H_3+R+T+W+A$  in columns  $C,\ldots,C+6$  occur below the two possible bar rows  $t,t+1\le23$ . Thus the statement for  $B\ge8$  does not rely only on the maximum-column bound; it also uses this row-local emptiness. That fact should be stated explicitly in a polished proof, but it follows from the displayed recursive source records and is not a counterexample.The parity facts are exactly the ones needed:
$$C,b,a,e\ \text{odd},\qquad t,J,v\ \text{even}.$$
Consequently, the frontier intervals have no missing equality case. In particular,  $J=e$  cannot occur because  $J$  is even and  $e$  is odd.2. Complete-owner normalization at  $p=(25,C)$ The retained endpoints at  $(25,C-1)$  and  $(25,C+1)$  force a fresh owner at  $p$  in any complete extension. The owner cannot be one of the retained originals because  $p$  is absent from their endpoint union.RotorsFor a rotor endpoint at  $p$ , the two horizontal neighbours are already occupied by retained endpoints. A degree-three rotor endpoint is therefore impossible. The remaining vertical-terminal patterns are the four north/south terminal cases, and each contains a point on P’s left wall. Hence no rotor can own  $p$ .This conclusion is invariant under the allowed lattice isometries. The transpose orientations do not provide an omitted case: a bar endpoint of a full  $U$  still has a horizontal internal endpoint neighbour after the isometry, and a rotated horizontal leg also has a horizontal internal neighbour.Full  $U$ A full  $U$  owning  $p$  cannot place  $p$  on a bar or on a horizontal leg, because one of those would give  $p$  a horizontal internal neighbour. Thus  $p$  lies on a vertical leg away from the bar.The retained endpoint at  $(31,C)$  prevents the leg from crossing row  $31$ . The horizontal companions retained by P and K exclude bar rows  $25,\ldots,30$ , and a bar above row  $30$  would force the leg through the retained point  $(31,C)$ . Therefore the leg is south-going, with bar row  $t$  and terminal row  $u$  satisfying
$$25\le u\le30.$$
Why  $u<30$  is impossible in a complete extensionSuppose  $u\le29$ . The next point
$$q=(u+1,C),\qquad 26\le q_{\rm row}\le30,$$
is the axial support beyond the owner’s leg tip. It is absent from the baseline endpoint union and from  $O$ .At  $q$ , the owner above supplies the north endpoint, while P and K supply the west and east retained endpoints. Thus  $q$  has more than one occupied neighbour. Under the support-consumption rule,  $q$  must be occupied as an endpoint by a distinct additional original. This is the point where the complete-extension hypothesis is used; endpoint disjointness alone does not force  $u=30$ .That additional owner can have only a south-pointing matching edge.If it is a full  $U$  with south leg depth  $k\ge4$  and  $q_{\rm row}\ge27$ , its continuous stem contains  $(31,C)$ , the retained Q endpoint.If  $q_{\rm row}=26$  and  $k\ge6$ , the same stem again contains  $(31,C)$ .The remaining full- $U$  case  $q_{\rm row}=26,k=4$  puts the new bar at row  $30$ , where both possible horizontal companions are occupied by P and K.A rotor with the only available south-terminal matching direction contains
$$(q_{\rm row}+2,C-1),$$
which is a P endpoint for  $q_{\rm row}=26,\ldots,30$ .Every allowed second owner is excluded. Hence  $u=30$ .Since the near leg depth is  $d=30-t$  and all depths are even,  $t$  is even. The case  $t=24$  places the inner bar row at  $25$ , where the retained horizontal neighbours again collide. Therefore
$$t\le22.$$
For a west-going bar,  $t=22$  additionally collides with P at  $(23,C-1)$ , so
$$t\le20$$
in the west form.After exchanging the two equal-parity legs when necessary, the only possible complete-extension owner records are exactly
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{EAST}:&\quad
O=U(B,30-t,f),\quad \operatorname{chart}(t+r,C-1+c),\\
\mathrm{WEST}:&\quad
O=U(B,30-t,f),\quad \operatorname{chart}(t+r,C+1-c),
\end{aligned}$$
with  $B,f\ge4$  even,  $B\ge6$ ,  $t\le22$ , and  $t\le20$  in the west case.3. Exact disjointness frontiersLet
$$v=t+f.$$
For the east form the far column is  $C+B-1$ . For the west form put
$$J=C+1-B.$$
The six frontier cases are exhaustive.Form and phaseExact disjointness restrictionSole possible far eventEast,  $B\ge8$ nonenoneEast,  $B=6$  $v\le24$  $v=24$ :  $K:(25,C+5)\to O:(24,C+5)$ West,  $J\ge b+1$  $v\le22$  $v=22$ :  $P:(23,J)\to O:(22,J)$ West,  $e+1\le J\le b-1$  $t\le a-3,\ v\le a-1$  $v=a-1$ :  $A:(a,J)\to O:(a-1,J)$ West,  $J\le e-1,\ J\ge-34$  $t\le a-3,\ v\le20$ noneWest,  $J\le e-1,\ J\le-36$  $t\le a-3$ noneThe reasons are exact:For  $B=6$ , the far column is  $C+5$ , and the first old endpoint there is K’s row- $25$  endpoint. The far leg therefore must stop at  $v\le24$ .For  $B\ge8$ , the far column begins at  $C+7$ , outside the old endpoint range. The previously noted row-local emptiness prevents a collision from the east bar itself.If  $J\ge b+1$ , the west bar lies entirely to the right of A. P’s first endpoint in the far column is at row  $23$ , giving  $v\le22$ .If  $e+1\le J\le b-1$ , the far leg crosses A’s far-leg interval. Since  $a$  is odd and  $t$  is even, avoiding A’s bar column requires exactly  $t\le a-3$ , and avoiding A’s far-leg endpoint at row  $a$  requires  $v\le a-1$ .If  $J\le e-1$  but  $J\ge-34$ , the first contact is the contiguous row- $22$  W/A union, so  $v\le20$ .If  $J\le-36$ , both the far column and its physical partner lie to the left of every old endpoint; no far restriction remains.The frontiers are therefore conditions for disjointness from the entire  $H$ , not merely from a selected local subset.4. New receipts and nonreuseThe near leg of  $O$  occupies column  $C$  from its bar through row  $30$ , while P occupies column  $C-1$  through the relevant interval. Exactly four newly completed mixed tiles appear:
$$(24,C-1),\quad (26,C-1),\quad (28,C-1),\quad (30,C-1).$$
The final tile is the  $P/O/Q$  tile:P supplies both left cells;O supplies  $(30,C)$ ;Q supplies  $(31,C)$ .It is one three-owner tile and is counted exactly once.The eight new near events are:
$$P:(r,C-1)\to O:(r,C),
\qquad r=24,26,28,30,$$
and:East:
$$O:(r,C)\to P:(r,C-1),
\qquad r=23,25,27,29;$$
West:
$$O:(r,C)\to P:(r,C-1),
\qquad r=24,26,28,30.$$
The phase difference is forced by the two support/matching parities of the reflected  $U$ -records.The existing Q-to-P event at row  $31$  is not new. The O-to-Q and Q-to-O directions at the bottom tile target the corresponding original axial supports and are excluded. The remaining directions at the near tiles likewise target original supports or are not intratile foreign events.The far contact contributes at most one new event, exactly in the three rows of the table above. Its reverse direction always targets O’s original axial support, so it is excluded from  $E$ . No far contact creates another full tile: in each frontier tile one of the other two cells remains absent.The near and far receipt sets are disjoint because the far column differs from the near column by  $B-1\ge5$ . The source-owner labels are also distinct:K supplies the east  $B=6$  far event;P supplies the west  $J\ge b+1$  event;A supplies the west returned-far event;O supplies the new near events.Thus no H3 reserve, A receipt, old event, or old full tile is counted again.5. Source charge and marginalWrite
$$d=30-t,\qquad x=\frac{d+f}{2}.$$
For the east form:
$$\begin{aligned}
\#\text{matching edges}&=B-1+x,\\
\#\text{endpoint tiles}&=\frac B2+1+x,\\
\#\text{internal supports}&=4+x.
\end{aligned}$$
Therefore
$$\operatorname{charge}(O)
=(B-1+x)+(4+x)-2\left(\frac B2+1+x\right)=+1.$$
For the west form:
$$\begin{aligned}
\#\text{matching edges}&=B-1+x,\\
\#\text{endpoint tiles}&=\frac B2+x,\\
\#\text{internal supports}&=x,
\end{aligned}$$
so
$$\operatorname{charge}(O)
=(B-1+x)+x-2\left(\frac B2+x\right)=-1.$$
In the east case,  $N$  increases by  $1$  and  $S$  does not change. In the west case,  $S$  increases by  $1$  and  $N$  does not change. Thus the source contributes  $+1$  to  $N+S$  in both orientations.With four new full tiles and  $8+\delta$  new directed events,
$$\Phi(H+O)-\Phi(H)
=1+2\cdot4-(8+\delta)
=1-\delta\ge0,$$
where  $\delta=1$  exactly in one of the three far-event phases and  $\delta=0$  otherwise.This proves the claimed nonnegative marginal for every actual root-support owner in a complete extension.6. Reach restriction for the preceding upward returnThe dependency corollary is also sound.For
$$A=U(L,D,F),\qquad \operatorname{chart}(23-c,7+D-r),$$
all A endpoints lie at rows at most  $22$ . If  $D\ge h+6$ , then A supplies the missing cap  $(22,C)$ :at  $D=h+6$ , the bar column is exactly  $b=C$ ;for  $D\ge h+8$ , the row- $22$  near leg spans through column  $C$ .Together with K, P, and the old  $D=B_0[4]$  cap at  $(31,C)$ , this realizes the four-original obstruction. The three holes  $(25,C),(28,C),(30,C)$  remain empty because A ends at row  $22$ . Therefore no complete extension can contain such an A.Since  $D$  is even,
$$D\le h+4.$$
For the allowed range, A has:
$$\operatorname{charge}(A)=+1,$$

$$\#\text{new full tiles}=\frac D2+1,$$

$$\#\text{new events}=\frac{3D}{2}+1.$$
Hence
$$\Delta\Phi(A)
=1+2\left(\frac D2+1\right)
-\left(\frac{3D}{2}+1\right)
=2-\frac D2.$$
The first A tile is the three-owner W/A/P tile, and the A/W directions there target original axial supports. The P/A events have exactly the stated parity phases, with no hidden H3/R/T contact.7. Joint budgetUsing the previously established baseline identities
$$\Phi(H_3)=h+33,$$

$$\Delta\Phi(R+T+W)=1,$$
and
$$\Delta\Phi(A)=2-\frac D2,$$
the new root owner gives
$$\Delta\Phi(O)=1-\delta.$$
Therefore
$$\Phi(H+O)-\Phi(H_3)
=1+\left(2-\frac D2\right)+(1-\delta)
=4-\frac D2-\delta.$$
Since  $D\le h+4$  and  $\delta\le1$ ,
$$\Phi(H+O)
=h+37-\frac D2-\delta
\ge h+37-\frac{h+4}{2}-1
=\frac h2+34.$$
The bound is a valid joint selected-union budget. It counts H3 once and does not reassign H3’s reserve to another return.The correct final scope is therefore:ACCEPT for the stated full- $U$ /rotor model;conditional on a complete extension;no arbitrary-grid catalogue exhaustion;no complete-extension existence theorem;no global monotonicity under later additions;no global  $5/6$  improvement;no claim that the remaining return families or the rectangular-grid equality problem are settled.The only wording changes I recommend are to make the two logical dependencies explicit:  $q$  is forced to be an endpoint of a distinct owner by the support-consumption rule, and  $u=30$  is a complete-extension consequence rather than a property of every endpoint-disjoint partial owner.
